messages:
Amelia: Heads-up — compliance wants a concrete list of KMS audit artifacts for SOC2 evidence. They want per-provider retention settings, export locations, and a minimal query set to show 'who used which key' for the last 12 months. Can we assemble quickly?
Jonah: I can dump a checklist. High level: CloudTrail events for AWS KMS, GCP Audit Logs (Admin + Data Access as needed), Azure KeyVault diagnostic logs. Also need export buckets with immutability/retention and ACLs.
Mira: For AWS specifically, make sure we include these events: 
```
eventSource=kms.amazonaws.com AND eventName IN (Encrypt,Decrypt,GenerateDataKey,GenerateDataKeyWithoutPlaintext,ReEncrypt,CreateKey,EnableKeyRotation,DisableKeyRotation,ScheduleKeyDeletion)
```
Jonah: Also capture CloudTrail "ConsoleLogin"/assume-role events that correlate who initiated the KMS operation (userIdentity) — auditors look for principal.identity and sourceIPAddress.
Samir: For GCP, we should export both Admin Activity (always on) and Data Access (only if enabled for KMS actions). Proposed filter for exported logs in GCS / BigQuery: 
```
resource.type="kms_keyring" AND (protoPayload.methodName:"Encrypt" OR protoPayload.methodName:"Decrypt" OR protoPayload.methodName:"GenerateKey" OR protoPayload.methodName:"CreateKeyVersion" OR protoPayload.methodName:"SetIamPolicy")
```
Mira: Azure Key Vault: enable diagnostic settings on each vault and send logs to a Storage account with soft-delete and immutability policy + to Log Analytics for queries. Query example for Azure Monitor (Kusto): 
```
AzureDiagnostics
| where ResourceProvider == "MICROSOFT.KEYVAULT"
| where OperationName contains "encrypt" or OperationName contains "decrypt" or OperationName contains "wrapKey" or OperationName contains "unwrapKey"
```
Amelia: Great. Compliance also asked how we prove envelope encryption usage — they want the app-level metadata that ties ciphertext back to the KMS-generated data key. What do we have for that?
Jonah: App-level rule: every encrypted blob must include header metadata: {key_id, key_version, envelope_version, encrypted_data_key_id}. We log GenerateDataKey responses (only metadata, not plaintext key) with requestIds and keyVersionId. Sample log line we can surface: 
```
app-service: ENCRYPT requestId=abc123 key_id=arn:aws:kms:...:key/abcd key_version=1 data_key_id=dk-789 status=SUCCESS
```
Mira: Important: redact any plaintext or base64-encoded data key material in logs. Only store key identifiers and request ids.
Samir: On rotation evidence — auditors want proof rotation actually happened and that old keys are still accessible for decryption or have been schedule-deleted. For AWS we can show CloudTrail events for EnableKeyRotation and CreateKey with KeyMetadata. Also we can show the kms:GetKeyRotationStatus API response snapshot. For GCP/Azure similar: GCP CryptoKeyVersions create timestamps, Azure has key versions in key vault.
SecurityBot: exported_logs: s3://redwood-security-audit/kms/2026/ ; gcs://redwood-kms-audit/2026/ ; az://redwood-audit/kms/2026/ - checksum manifests generated: manifest-2026-03-01.sha256
Amelia: Perfect. Compliance also wants a sample query set they can run to demonstrate "who used key X between dates Y and Z". Can we provide short examples?
Jonah: AWS Athena (on CloudTrail Parquet): 
```
SELECT eventTime, eventName, userIdentity, sourceIPAddress, requestParameters
FROM cloudtrail_logs
WHERE eventSource = 'kms.amazonaws.com'
  AND requestParameters.keyId = 'arn:aws:kms:...(key-id)...'
  AND eventTime BETWEEN '2025-03-01' AND '2026-03-01';
```
Mira: GCP BigQuery example: 
```
SELECT timestamp, protoPayload.methodName, protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail, resource.labels.key_ring, protoPayload.request
FROM `project.dataset.cloudaudit_googleapis_com_activity_*`
WHERE resource.type = 'kms_keyring'
  AND protoPayload.methodName IN ('Encrypt','Decrypt','GenerateKey')
  AND timestamp BETWEEN '2025-03-01' AND '2026-03-01';
```
Samir: Azure Log Analytics: 
```
AzureDiagnostics
| where Resource == '/SUBSCRIPTIONS/.../resourceGroups/.../providers/Microsoft.KeyVault/vaults/my-vault'
| where OperationName has_any ("encrypt","decrypt","wrapKey","unwrapKey")
| where TimeGenerated between (datetime(2025-03-01) .. datetime(2026-03-01))
| project TimeGenerated, OperationName, CallerIpAddress, Identity
```
Compliance: Quick Q — do we have retention windows pinned? SOC2 wants 12 months minimum for security logs, some customers want 36 months.
Amelia: Current defaults: CloudTrail (90d in live) + long-term to S3 with 7 years lifecycle for archived bucket. GCP logs -> BigQuery export with table partitioning + 7y. Azure -> Storage account with immutable blob storage 7y and Log Analytics retention 365d (we need to export to storage for >1y).
Jonah: Action item: update runbook to show exact buckets and lifecycle policies, plus screenshots of Console/CLI commands that set retention. Also capture IAM policies for read-only access to the audit exports.
Mira: Note for cross-cloud correlation: ensure exported logs include a consistent field with our internal customer/tenant id when available (our app should emit metadata). Otherwise mapping principals across clouds will be manual.
Samir: Evidence packaging checklist I propose: 
1) manifest.csv listing exported files (path, sha256, size, dateRange)
2) retention_policy.png (console screenshot) or CLI output for lifecycle rules
3) key_rotation_log.txt (CloudTrail/GCP/Azure entries showing rotation events)
4) sample_queries.sql (Athena/BigQuery/Kusto)
5) app_encryption_metadata_sample.txt (example header/log line)
6) access_list.csv (who has read access to exported logs)
7) signed_hashes and storage ACL screenshots
Amelia: That looks good. Compliance also asked for an example of how we prove an old key was used to decrypt older ciphertext after rotation. Any short explainer?
Jonah: Short: rotation creates a new key version but does not delete old versions by default. Show key version list (AWS: ListKeyVersions/GetPublicKey?), show Decrypt events referencing old keyVersionId, and show app logs where encrypted_data_key_id points to old version. Provide a timeline: encryption (t1) -> rotation (t2) -> decryption (t3) with logs showing t3 referencing t1 key id.
Mira: I'll assemble the CLI commands and small playbook. Example AWS CLI snapshot for rotation status: 
```
aws kms get-key-rotation-status --key-id arn:aws:kms:...:key/abcd
```
SecurityBot: note: exported bucket s3://redwood-security-audit/kms/2026/ has object lock enabled and a 7-year retention policy applied on 2026-03-01 by iam-user:sys-ops.
Compliance: Thanks — please drop the runbook and the sample manifests into the compliance folder and ping us when done. :thumbsup:
Amelia: Will do. I'll create the artifacts and post links here once uploaded.
Jonah: I'll write the sample queries and test them against last year's partition.
Mira: I'll handle Azure/ GCP export snapshots and the app metadata sample.
Samir: I'll verify rotation evidence and generate the key-version timelines.
Amelia: Thanks everyone. Low-priority follow-up: make a short one-page note for customer-facing teams explaining what artifacts we can provide on demand and SLAs for retrieval.
